## Claim — `domain:ui` execution seat

Session `session_01EMrWaQw3XS5DxTHxp4yRyC`. Branch `claude/issue-7129-retire-detailviewsection-hideempty`. Dispatching now.

Authority: comment [5494797031](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/7129#issuecomment-5494797031) (项目总监席, 总监批 #28, 2026-09-01, maintainer verbatim 「同意」) — **Q1-A / Q2-C**, retire `DetailViewSection.hideEmpty`. Clause ② **yes**; the PR carries `needs:contract-review`, stays draft, ⛔ no self-review or enqueue by this seat.

⚠️ This card's title begins `[Decision]` and its body poses an open question. It was answered on 2026-09-01. I had it parked as undispatchable on exactly that reading — the fourth card in this batch I got wrong the same way.

### ⭐⭐ Three same-named surfaces, all measured — a bare `grep hideEmpty` walks into every one

| what a grep returns | is it the target? |
|---|---|
| `hideEmptyFields` — ten locale packs, `useDetailTranslation.ts:106`, `DetailSection.tsx:518` | ⛔ **No** — a different key, an i18n label. Prefix match. |
| `record-reference-rail.tsx:54/232/241` `hideEmpty?: boolean` | ⛔ **No** — the reference rail, a different surface. The ruling retires only `DetailViewSection`. |
| `views.ts:229`, `record-details.tsx:235`, `plugin-detail/index.tsx:750` | ✅ **Yes** |

All three are in the brief by name. The dev is also asked to establish which surface `DetailSection.tsx:179-198` belongs to and to hand the question back rather than guess if it is genuinely ambiguous.

### ⚠️ The compile-time ledger will bite — and that is expected, not scope creep

`packages/types/src/__tests__/zod-mirror-parity.test.ts:1057` carries a `views.zod.ts#DetailViewSectionSchema` `KnownDrift` entry. That ledger is enforced at compile time (`export const assertionDriftMatchesLedger: never`) and, by its own header, *"fails when new drift appears on that mirror AND when the recorded drift is fixed."* So retiring this key will very likely redden `packages/types` type-check until the entry is corrected.

⭐ This is the **third** card this shift where a census/ledger file must move with the change and is unreachable by grepping the symbol — after `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` on #6940 and the absolute member count in `useObjectLabel-identity-5564.test.tsx` on #7219. The brief says so up front so the dev does not read the red as its own bug, and does not treat correcting it as widening the PR.

Measured for the brief: the two unlanded PRs that also touch that file (#7432 at the `blocks.zod.ts` region, #7447 at `data-display.zod.ts#DataTableSchema`) are **disjoint** from a `views.zod.ts` region.

### File surface

**Zero collisions** across #7432 (23 files), #7447 (4), #7451 (5), #7332 (88), #7391 (33), #7400 (13), #7442 (8) — each total non-zero, so the zeros are readings.

PR #7123's behaviour pin is **restated, not deleted** — it asserts the key no longer exists, and its controls stay, per point 4 of the ruling. #7127 goes separately and is fenced out.

State transition, same stroke: `pm:queue` → `pm:dispatched`, assignee set.
